editorial.subjectLine: AI at MYOB, and a hackathon you can enter solo
editorial.previewText: You don't need a team or an AI background for 7–8 August — solo registrants get matched on the day.

founderNote.heading: A note from our founder
founderNote.bodyMd:
This week we ran Working Smarter with MYOB at their Albert Street office. We opened with a karakia, then three of their team spoke — Jean Fulop on product, Marion Nicholas on practice, Katy Seel on the people side. After that everyone split into small groups to work a real problem, with MYOB mentors circulating.

She Sharp is a partner in the [Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival](https://aihackathon.nz/) this year. It runs 7–8 August at AUT City Campus, two days building AI projects for the UN Sustainable Development Goals. I'll be one of the judges, so if you enter, I'll see your pitch.

We don't know yet who's coming. That's the only part of this that isn't sorted, and it's the part I care about.
founderNote.signature: Dr. Mahsa McCauley, Founder & Chair, She Sharp

headline.blurb: Friday evening through Saturday at AUT City Campus. Teams of three to seven take on a UN Sustainable Development Goal, with mentors and technical support in the room. Beginners are welcome. Winning teams go on to pitch at the Aotearoa AI Summit.

photoOfTheMonth.caption: Working Smarter under way at MYOB's Albert Street office, with three of their team on what AI has changed for them.

editorial.recapIntro: Just the one event in July.

eventBlurbs.she-sharp-and-myob-working-smarter: The second half was the point: teams of up to six, problem statements pitched at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels, and MYOB people moving between the tables to unstick them.

opportunities.title: Read up on mentoring
opportunities.body: Applications for this cohort closed in June and we don't have a date for the next round yet. What mentees ask for is someone one step ahead of them, not twenty years ahead. The role description is there now if you've been thinking about it.

opportunities.title: Volunteer with us
opportunities.body: Every event needs facilitators, floor helpers, and people who notice the newcomer standing on their own and go over. August's hackathon is the next big one.

opportunities.title: Support the mahi
opportunities.body: Our events are free, or close to it. Donations are why. If She Sharp has been useful to you at some point, this is the way to pass it on.

editorial.sponsorThanks: Thanks to MYOB for hosting us on Albert Street, and for giving us three of their leaders and a group of their mentors for the night. Thanks also to AUT and the AI Forum New Zealand, who are behind the 7–8 August hackathon we're part of.

heroStat.label: more NZ job ads mention AI skills than a year ago
heroStat.context: More than doubled in twelve months. If you've been wondering whether this is worth giving up a weekend for, that's your answer.

newsBites.title: If you shelved a job search, take it back off the shelf
newsBites.summary: Tech job ads are up 9.9% on a year ago and Auckland is up 5.0%, while ads nationally rose just 0.2% in June. Tech is growing faster than the market around it.

newsBites.title: The environmental bill for AI is becoming a public question
newsBites.summary: Telco One NZ surveyed 1,001 people: 45% are worried about the environmental impact of businesses using AI, rising to 63% among 18 to 24 year olds. Electricity use topped the list at 66%.

newsBites.title: Parents aren't sure their kids can spot a fake
newsBites.summary: Norton surveyed 1,000 New Zealand adults with children under 18. 44% weren't confident their child could tell AI-generated content from the real thing, and 37% doubted their child knew AI can be wrong. That gap is what schools outreach exists to close.

didYouKnow.text: NZ's tech 'skills shortage' is mostly a mismatch. The deepest unmet demand is for senior, experienced people — and the mentors we most need are the ones who assume they aren't senior enough.

recapEvents.title: Working Smarter: AI, MYOB, and the New Delivery Landscape
recapEvents.shortDescription: An interactive evening exploring how MYOB teams use AI to work smarter, solve problems faster, and deliver more value — with practical use cases and a hands-on AI problem-solving activity.
